answer: Each agent identity must lock a real balance, and peers attest only to staked work, so a farm of fresh wallets starts with zero trust. An attacker has to fund every fake from one source; the ledger clusters identities by funding root and freezes rewards, leaving each clone a violet mark. Cost also grows in a spiral: escrowed capital idles for many rounds before earning, so expense per surviving fake rises with duplicates. An honest operator at the wharf pays once and builds standing; a swarm pays thousands of times, making the attack uneconomic long before it looks small.
